Retro Webpage is a full-hearted celebration of the classic personal homepage, complete with colorful browser chrome, familiar boxy layout conventions, and the irresistible handmade charm of a site that was clearly built with love. It's the theme you reach for when you want your portfolio to feel like it was posted to a web ring and proudly linked from a GeoCities neighborhood.

## Theme Overview

Retro Webpage draws directly from the visual grammar of personal homepages from the mid-to-late 1990s: colorful browser-style chrome wrapping each content area, table-inspired layout conventions, bold decorative accents, and a general sense that every element was placed with enthusiasm rather than restraint. The result is a portfolio that feels genuinely warm and personable — an internet artifact from an era when having your own website was an act of self-expression as much as professional presentation. The design is carefully constructed to feel nostalgic without feeling broken.

## Design Highlights

- Colorful browser chrome framing that anchors the retro personal-homepage aesthetic
- Old-web layout conventions drawn from mid-1990s personal site design
- Bold decorative accents and vivid color that communicate handcrafted personality
- Content sections that echo the informal, enthusiasm-driven structure of early personal pages
- A warm, inviting visual tone that balances nostalgia with portfolio practicality

## Who This Theme Suits

Retro Webpage is perfect for developers, hobbyists, and digital creatives who have deep affection for internet history and want their portfolio to lead with personality. It suits front-end developers, indie web advocates, and anyone whose professional identity is as much about how they approach the work as what they've built — people who think the early web got some things very right.

<Tip>
  Lean into the theme's handcrafted spirit by writing your bio in a casual, first-person voice — Retro Webpage rewards content that matches its warm, personal-homepage energy.
</Tip>
